blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — clevidipine contraindication in severe aortic stenosis
stem: A client with severe aortic stenosis has a new order for IV clevidipine to rapidly lower blood pressure. Which action should the nurse take before starting the infusion?

options.A: Clarify the clevidipine order because severe aortic stenosis is a labeled contraindication; rapid arterial afterload reduction can reduce myocardial oxygen delivery.
options.B: Start clevidipine because it raises systemic vascular resistance, which supports coronary perfusion and improves forward flow across a severely stenotic aortic valve.
options.C: Start clevidipine because its main hemodynamic action is venoconstriction rather than arterial vasodilation, so severe aortic stenosis does not create added risk.
options.D: Question clevidipine only when renal clearance is impaired because the drug depends on kidney excretion and cannot be rapidly metabolized by circulating or tissue esterases.

rationale: Current CLEViprex labeling lists severe aortic stenosis as a contraindication because afterload reduction can be expected to reduce myocardial oxygen delivery. Clevidipine is a dihydropyridine L-type calcium-channel blocker that lowers blood pressure mainly by decreasing systemic vascular resistance, and it is rapidly hydrolyzed by esterases in blood and extravascular tissues rather than depending on renal clearance. Therefore A is correct. B, C, and D misstate its hemodynamic action or elimination.
educational_objective: Identify severe aortic stenosis as a contraindication to IV clevidipine and relate the risk to rapid arterial afterload reduction.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_document_title: CLEViprex (clevidipine) injectable emulsion — Full Prescribing Information

source_locator: Contraindications §4.3 Severe Aortic Stenosis: contraindicated because afterload reduction can reduce myocardial oxygen delivery. Clinical Pharmacology §§12.1-12.3: L-type calcium-channel blockade decreases systemic vascular resistance; clevidipine is rapidly hydrolyzed primarily by esterases in blood and extravascular tissues.
source_claim_supported: Clevidipine is contraindicated in severe aortic stenosis because afterload reduction can reduce myocardial oxygen delivery; its antihypertensive action is arterial vasodilation with rapid esterase metabolism.

candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices without absolute-word distractor cues.
Balanced option lengths and retained the exact labeled contraindication and mechanism.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches CLEViprex §4.3. All options are closely length-matched and no second defensible answer remains.
